productionErrorInvestigation.note: Operator reported hitting a 'model error' and a 'sign in again' error on production (skills-framework.fly.dev) roughly 10-20 minutes before being asked to check. The exact log lines were unrecoverable: the production machine restarted at 2026-10-06T18:01:14Z (splc-s1's own promotion to prod) before the check could run, fly logs --no-tail only covers the current boot's buffer, and no external log aggregator is configured (.github/context.yml has no tools.log_aggregation) to retain history across restarts. Traced both error strings in code instead -- 'Model error -- please try again.' (src/web-ui/routes/skills.js:5382, generic catch-all on any SSE/LLM turn exception after one auto-retry; real cause logged server-side as event:sse_error, which was lost) and 'Session expired -- sign in again' (skills.js:3946/4104, client-side inference whenever a turn-submit response is ok but not an actual SSE stream -- almost always an expired session cookie). A fresher log pull (current boot, last ~5-10 min at the time) found 2 real sse_client_disconnect WARN events plus one abnormally slow 170-second LLM turn (llm_duration_ms:170146) -- a plausible but NOT confirmed explanation (a turn that looked hung from the client's side, possibly compounded by the session cookie expiring during the long wait). Checked PostHog (Error Tracking + raw event explorer, last hour) and found nothing, then confirmed via code read why: skills.js's error paths never call into PostHog at all -- a real, confirmed instrumentation gap, not just an unobserved event. Separately, a DIFFERENT real, currently-repeating bug WAS confirmed (unrelated to the above): every login triggers [auth] tenant_admin_bootstrap_failed with reason 'inconsistent types deduced for parameter $1' for tenantId heymishy -- does not block login, but is a live SQL type-inference defect firing on every single sign-in. None of these were fixed or scoped as stories. At the operator's suggestion, registered PostHog's official hosted MCP server (claude mcp add --transport http posthog https://mcp.posthog.com/mcp -s user) to replace browser automation for this kind of investigation going forward. OAuth could not be completed via the agent's own non-interactive Bash tool (consistent with the standing boundary against driving third-party OAuth); the operator ran `claude mcp login posthog` themselves and it is now Connected per `claude mcp list`. However its tools did not appear via ToolSearch in the already-running session -- MCP servers load at session start, so the operator is restarting specifically to pick them up.
